question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in generic adaptive inbound debounce policy, keep fixed debounce as the supported baseline, or require a channel/plugin API seam before adding smarter timing?
rationale: The request adds public config and changes how inbound fragments become one agent turn, so automation cannot safely choose increment/max, count-trigger, typing-signal, default, transcript, and channel ownership semantics.

options.title: Design generic adaptive debounce
options.body: Add an opt-in core or SDK-backed policy with typed config, schema/docs, current-default preservation, and tests for fixed, incremental, capped, and channel-specific behavior.

options.title: Keep fixed debounce baseline
options.body: Document messages.inbound.debounceMs and byChannel as the supported batching answer and close or defer adaptive timing unless stronger demand appears.

options.title: Require plugin/API seam first
options.body: Defer implementation until channel plugins can expose reliable typing or composition signals without growing core message config prematurely.

recommendation.title: Design generic adaptive debounce
recommendation.body: Add an opt-in core or SDK-backed policy with typed config, schema/docs, current-default preservation, and tests for fixed, incremental, capped, and channel-specific behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across shared inbound debounce policy, docs, and product-review context for this surface.
